node.label: Listen address
node.help: Where the server waits for clients, for example 0.0.0.0:7835, or just a port such as 7835 for every IPv4 address

node.label: Public address
node.help: How clients reach this server, for example tunnel.example.com, or wss://tunnel.example.com/burrow when WebSocket is on; connect commands made here use it

node.label: WebSocket listener
node.help: Accept clients over WebSocket, for servers reachable only through HTTP(S)

node.label: Listen address
node.help: Address to accept WebSocket connections on, for example 127.0.0.1:7836 behind a proxy; a port alone means 0.0.0.0

node.label: Path
node.help: URL path clients connect to, for example /burrow

node.label: Name on the HTTPS port
node.help: The name that leads to the tunnel when it shares the web proxy's HTTPS port, for example tunnel.example.com

node.label: TLS
node.help: Serve wss:// directly with these PEM files instead of behind a TLS proxy

node.label: Certificate file
node.help: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem

node.label: Private key file
node.help: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

node.label: Keepalive
node.help: Seconds between keepalives on idle pooled channels, below your proxy's idle timeout

node.label: Let's Encrypt check
node.help: How Let's Encrypt checks the tunnel's own name, for example http behind a proxy that does the HTTPS

options.label: TLS
options.help: Let's Encrypt connects to the HTTPS port; needs web.https on 443

options.label: HTTP
options.help: Let's Encrypt fetches a file over plain HTTP; needs web.http on 80

options.label: DNS
options.help: Let's Encrypt reads a DNS record that burrow sets through web.letsencrypt.dns; no open port needed

node.label: Web proxy
node.help: The web proxy: one HTTPS port for websites and TLS services by name; off unless set

node.label: HTTPS port
node.help: The port where websites and TLS services are reached by name, for example 443; a port alone listens on IPv4 and IPv6, 0.0.0.0:443 on IPv4 only

node.label: HTTP port
node.help: The port for plain HTTP, for example 80: sites with HTTPS off, the step from http:// to https:// and Let's Encrypt's check; a port alone listens on IPv4 and IPv6

node.label: Send http:// to https://
node.help: For every HTTPS website: send a visitor who types http://example.com to https://example.com, or answer plain HTTP too; a website can change it

node.label: HTTP/2
node.help: Let browsers use HTTP/2 on the HTTPS port, faster for pages with many parts; turn it off only for a client that breaks with it

node.label: Login service
node.help: The single sign-on service websites can share to check their visitors, for example Authelia

node.label: Service
node.help: The service of the login portal that checks each visitor, for example authelia

node.label: Path
node.help: Where the login service answers the check, for example /api/authz/forward-auth for Authelia or /outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/nginx for authentik

node.label: Headers to the app
node.help: Headers from the login service's answer that the app receives, for example Remote-User; a visitor's own copies are always removed

node.label: Rate limit
node.help: For every website: how many requests per second one visitor may send, for example 20; a website can change it

node.label: Let's Encrypt
node.help: Automatic certificates for every website name no file covers; turning it on accepts Let's Encrypt's terms, for example with the email ops@example.com

node.label: Email
node.help: Let's Encrypt's contact for this server, for example ops@example.com; giving it accepts Let's Encrypt's terms

node.label: Certificate service
node.help: Where certificates come from: Let's Encrypt, its test service for trying things out, or another ACME server by its directory URL, for example https://ca.internal/acme/directory

options.label: Staging
options.help: Let's Encrypt's test service: higher limits, certificates browsers do not trust

node.label: Trusted CA file
node.help: The CA certificate to trust for another ACME server, for example certs/internal-ca.pem

node.label: Uploaded trusted CA
node.help: The CA certificate to trust for another ACME server, uploaded here

node.label: Certificate profile
node.help: The kind of certificate to ask for, for example shortlived for 6-day certificates; IP addresses always use it

node.label: DNS checks
node.help: How burrow sets DNS records for Let's Encrypt's DNS check, needed for wildcards and names not reachable from the internet; each provider lists the domains it manages, for example example.com through Cloudflare

node.label: Domains
node.help: The domains whose DNS records this provider can set, for example example.com; it covers every name under it, like wiki.example.com and *.apps.example.com

node.label: Cloudflare
node.help: Cloudflare sets the records, with an API token allowed Zone:Read and DNS:Edit on these zones only

node.label: API token
node.help: An API token allowed Zone:Read and DNS:Edit on these zones only, from an environment variable like ${CF_TOKEN} or a file like file:/etc/burrow/cf.token

node.label: RFC 2136 (BIND, Knot, PowerDNS)
node.help: Your own DNS server sets the records by dynamic update signed with a TSIG key

node.label: Server
node.help: The zone's primary nameserver with its port, for example 192.168.1.2:53; it may be on the LAN if it feeds the public nameservers

node.label: Key name
node.help: The TSIG key's name, as in the server's key file, for example burrow-key

node.label: Key secret
node.help: The TSIG secret in base64, as in the server's key file, from an environment variable like ${TSIG_SECRET} or a file like file:/etc/burrow/tsig.secret

node.label: Algorithm
node.help: The TSIG key's algorithm, as in the server's key file, for example hmac-sha512

node.label: acme-dns
node.help: An acme-dns server sets the records; each name's _acme-challenge is a CNAME to it

node.label: Server address
node.help: The acme-dns server's address, for example https://auth.example.org

node.label: User name
node.help: The acme-dns account's user name, from an environment variable like ${ACMEDNS_USER} or a file

node.label: Password
node.help: The acme-dns account's password, from an environment variable like ${ACMEDNS_KEY} or a file

node.label: Subdomain
node.help: The account's subdomain, which each name's _acme-challenge CNAME points to, for example d420c923-bbd7-4056-ab64-c3ca54c9b3cf

node.label: Command
node.help: A program that sets the records with any provider, called with present or cleanup, the record's name and its value, for example /usr/local/bin/burrow-dns

node.label: Shared wildcards
node.help: One certificate each for every site one label under it and its parent name, for example *.example.com

node.label: Wait for the record
node.help: How long burrow waits for every nameserver of the zone to answer the new record, for example 120 seconds

node.label: Resolvers
node.help: Only used to find the zone's public nameservers, which burrow then asks directly, for example 1.1.1.1; they must give the public view

node.label: Certificate files
node.help: Your own certificate files, each used for exactly the names it lists, for example *.example.com with certs/wild.pem and certs/wild.key

node.label: Host names
node.help: The names this file is used for, for example *.example.com and example.com; the certificate must cover each

node.label: Certificate file
node.help: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem

node.label: Private key file
node.help: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

node.label: Uploaded certificate
node.help: A certificate with its private key, uploaded here and kept in burrow's state folder

node.label: Request header timeout
node.help: How long a visitor may take to send a request's headers, and how long an idle kept-alive connection stays open, for example 10 seconds

node.label: Idle timeout
node.help: A connection that moves no data for this long is closed, for example 60 seconds; WebSockets stay open

node.label: Names that only redirect
node.help: A name with no site of its own that sends visitors elsewhere, path and query kept, for example old.example.com to https://example.com, or example.com/shop to https://shop.example.net/

node.label: Send to
node.help: A full address or a path on the same name, for example https://example.com/new or /new; the rest of the path and the query are kept

node.label: Permanent
node.help: Browsers remember a permanent redirect, so use it only when you are sure

node.label: Trusted proxies
node.help: HTTP proxies in front of burrow, like Cloudflare, whose X-Forwarded-For tells the visitor's address, for example 173.245.48.0/20; behind cloudflared, its own address like 127.0.0.1/32

node.label: PROXY headers from
node.help: Load balancers in front of burrow that send a PROXY header with the visitor's address, for example 10.0.0.5/32; they must send it, and nobody else may

node.label: Access log
node.help: One line per request, written to a file, for example logs/access.log, in the common format or as JSON

node.label: File
node.help: Where each request is written, one line each, for example logs/access.log

node.label: Format
node.help: common is one line like nginx and Apache write; json suits log tools

options.label: Common
options.help: One line per request, like nginx and Apache

options.label: JSON
options.help: One JSON object per line, for log tools

node.label: Request ids
node.help: Give each request an X-Request-Id that the app, the visitor and the access log all see; one from a trusted proxy is kept

node.label: HSTS
node.help: For every HTTPS website: tell browsers to use only HTTPS for a year; a website can change it

node.label: Compress
node.help: For every website: gzip text answers like HTML, CSS and JSON when the browser accepts it; a website can change it

node.label: Biggest upload
node.help: For every website: the biggest request body, for example 100MB; bigger uploads get 413; a website can change it

node.label: App answer timeout
node.help: For every website: how long the app may take to start its answer before the visitor gets 504, for example 60 seconds; a website can change it

node.label: Request headers
node.help: For every website: headers set on requests to the app, for example X-Frame-Options: DENY; an empty value removes one

value.help: The header's value, for example DENY; empty removes the header

node.label: Answer headers
node.help: For every website: headers set on answers, for example X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; an empty value like Server: "" removes one

value.help: The header's value, for example DENY; empty removes the header

node.label: Error pages
node.help: For every website: a folder with your own pages, for example pages/, holding any of 404.html, 413.html, 429.html, 502.html, 503.html, 504.html and maintenance.html; the rest stay built in

node.label: Clients
node.help: Clients allowed to connect

node.label: Secrets
node.help: Secrets this client may sign in with; it has several only during a rotation

node.label: Max connections on this server
node.help: Connections this server forwards to the client at once. The client has its own limit too, max_connections in its client.yaml

node.label: Visitors
node.help: Visitors allowed to reach private services with burrow visit

node.label: Secrets
node.help: Secrets this visitor may sign in with; it has several only during a rotation

node.label: Direct access to clients
node.help: Clients this visitor may reach directly, over TCP and UDP: any target the client allows, or only those listed, for example 10.0.0.5:22 or 192.168.150.0/25

node.label: Max connections
node.help: Maximum concurrent connections for this visitor

node.label: Admin access
node.help: Let this visitor administer the server with burrow admin: read shows the dashboard and the config, write may also change it

options.label: Read
options.help: Dashboard, config with secrets as fingerprints, history

options.label: Write
options.help: Everything read gives, and changing the config

node.label: Admin only from
node.help: Admin access only from these addresses or networks, for example 203.0.113.0/24 or 10.0.0.0/8; any address when empty

groups.label: Admin access
groups.sub: May this visitor run burrow admin against this server?

node.label: This server
node.help: Targets this server may reach itself, for services that run on this server and visitors that reach it directly

node.label: Allowed targets
node.help: Addresses this server may reach itself, for example 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.10:22 or unix:/run/app.sock; link-local and cloud metadata addresses only when listed one by one

node.none_label: Only the targets of its own services

node.label: Services
node.help: Services this server exposes

node.label: Client
node.help: Name of the client that reaches the target

node.label: Clients
node.help: Clients that can each reach the target; with two or more, Mode appears to choose how one is picked

node.label: Mode
node.help: With several clients: failover uses the first one that is up, balance spreads new connections over all of them

options.label: Failover
options.help: Use the first client that is up

options.label: Balance
options.help: Spread new connections over all clients

relations.reason: UDP services do not support this

node.label: Health check
node.help: Check that each client can reach the target, and send connections only to those that can

node.label: Interval
node.help: Seconds between checks of each client

node.label: Timeout
node.help: Seconds a check may take

node.label: Failures before down
node.help: Failed checks in a row before a client counts as down

node.label: Path to check
node.help: For a website: ask the app for this path through each client, for example /healthz; an answer of 2xx or 3xx counts as up, and the path must not need a login

relations.reason: UDP services do not support this

node.label: Public address
node.help: The address and port the server opens for this service, for example 8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080

node.label: Target on the client
node.help: Where the client connects, as seen from the client, for example 127.0.0.1:3000 or 10.0.0.5:22; a port alone means the client itself

node.label: Protocol
node.help: TCP for most services; UDP for DNS, WireGuard or game servers

node.label: Max connections
node.help: Maximum concurrent connections for this service

relations.reason: UDP services do not support this

node.label: Visitors
node.help: Visitors that may reach this service with burrow visit

node.label: Allow from
node.help: Only these addresses or networks may connect, for example 203.0.113.0/24 or 10.0.0.0/8

node.label: Deny from
node.help: Addresses or networks that may never connect, for example 198.51.100.7 or 198.51.100.0/24

node.label: PROXY protocol
node.help: Send the real source address to the target with the PROXY protocol, v1 (text) or v2 (binary); only for targets that expect it

relations.reason: UDP services do not support this

node.label: Speed limit
node.help: Speed limit in each direction, shared by all connections of this service, for example 40mbit or 5MB per second

node.label: Website
node.help: Names that lead to this service on the web proxy's HTTPS port, for example nas.example.com

node.label: Host names
node.help: Names that lead to this service, for example nas.example.com, *.apps.example.com or 203.0.113.10

node.label: HTTPS
node.help: Who does HTTPS for this website: burrow with an automatic certificate, the app itself (burrow only reads the name), nobody (plain HTTP), burrow with its local CA for names on your network, or burrow with your own certificate

options.label: Automatic
options.help: burrow does HTTPS with a certificate for every name

options.label: The app does its own HTTPS
options.help: The app keeps its own certificate; burrow only reads the name

options.label: Off: plain HTTP
options.help: No HTTPS: the website is served as plain HTTP

options.label: Local CA, for names on your network
options.help: burrow's own certificate authority signs certificates for names like nas.lan; install its certificate on your devices once

node.label: Certificate file
node.help: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem; with key, or upload instead

node.label: Private key file
node.help: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

node.label: Uploaded certificate
node.help: A certificate with its private key, uploaded here and kept in burrow's state folder

node.label: Send http:// to https://
node.help: Send a visitor who types http://nas.example.com to https://nas.example.com, or answer plain HTTP too

node.label: Let's Encrypt check
node.help: How Let's Encrypt checks that the names are yours: over HTTP for a site behind Cloudflare's proxy, for example; automatic tries TLS on port 443 first, then HTTP on port 80

options.label: TLS
options.help: Let's Encrypt connects to the HTTPS port; needs web.https on 443

options.label: HTTP
options.help: Let's Encrypt fetches a file over plain HTTP; needs web.http on 80

options.label: DNS
options.help: Let's Encrypt reads a DNS record that burrow sets through web.letsencrypt.dns; no open port needed

node.label: Paths
node.help: Only these paths on the names lead here, each with everything below it, for example /api for /api and /api/users but not /apix; the longest match wins

node.label: Path on the app
node.help: What the app sees in place of the matched path, for example /v1 sends /api/users as /v1/users, and / removes /api

node.label: Redirect from
node.help: Names that send visitors to the first host name for good, path kept, for example www.example.com

node.label: Redirects
node.help: Paths that send visitors elsewhere, the rest of the path and the query kept, for example /old to /new or to https://example.net/new

node.label: Send to
node.help: A full address or a path on the same name, for example https://example.com/new or /new; the rest of the path and the query are kept

node.label: Permanent
node.help: Browsers remember a permanent redirect, so use it only when you are sure

node.label: Maintenance
node.help: Answer every visitor with the maintenance page instead of the app

node.label: HTTPS to the app
node.help: For an app that speaks HTTPS itself: check its certificate against the public CAs or your own CA, or not at all for a self-made one like Proxmox's

node.label: CA file
node.help: The CA that signed the app's certificate, for example certs/corp-ca.pem

node.label: Uploaded CA
node.help: The CA that signed the app's certificate, uploaded here

node.label: Skip the certificate check
node.help: For apps with a self-made certificate, like Proxmox, UniFi or DSM

node.none_label: Off: plain HTTP to the app

node.label: HTTP/2 to the app
node.help: Speak HTTP/2 to the app, needed for gRPC: without HTTPS to the app it is plain h2c, with it h2 inside TLS

node.label: Passwords
node.help: Visitors sign in with a user name and password, for example alice with a hash from burrow passwd alice

value.help: The password hash, for example the line burrow passwd alice prints

node.label: Login service
node.help: Visitors log in at a single sign-on service like Authelia or authentik before they reach the app

node.label: Service
node.help: The service of the login portal that checks each visitor, for example authelia

node.label: Path
node.help: Where the login service answers the check, for example /api/authz/forward-auth for Authelia or /outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/nginx for authentik

node.label: Headers to the app
node.help: Headers from the login service's answer that the app receives, for example Remote-User; a visitor's own copies are always removed

node.label: Rate limit
node.help: How many requests per second one visitor may send, for example 20; more get 429

node.label: Device certificates
node.help: Only devices with a certificate from your own CA may open the site, for example company laptops

node.label: CA file
node.help: The CA that signs your devices' certificates, with its intermediates, for example certs/devices-ca.pem

node.label: Uploaded CA
node.help: The CA that signs your devices' certificates, with its intermediates, uploaded here

node.label: Revocation list
node.help: Devices you revoked, as the CA publishes them, for example certs/devices.crl; re-read when the file changes

node.label: Uploaded revocation list
node.help: Devices you revoked, as the CA publishes them, uploaded here; upload a new list to replace it

node.label: HSTS
node.help: Tell browsers to use only HTTPS for this site for a year

node.label: Compress
node.help: Gzip text answers like HTML, CSS and JSON when the browser accepts it

node.label: Biggest upload
node.help: The biggest request body, for example 8GB for ISO uploads; bigger uploads get 413

node.label: App answer timeout
node.help: How long the app may take to start its answer before the visitor gets 504, for example 300 seconds for slow reports

node.label: Request headers
node.help: Headers set on requests to the app, for example Host: app.internal for an app that wants its own name; an empty value removes one

value.help: The header's value, for example DENY; empty removes the header

node.label: Answer headers
node.help: Headers set on answers, for example Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://example.com for CORS; an empty value removes one

value.help: The header's value, for example DENY; empty removes the header

node.label: Error pages
node.help: A folder with this site's own pages, for example pages/shop/, holding any of 404.html, 413.html, 429.html, 502.html, 503.html, 504.html and maintenance.html; the rest stay built in

relations.reason: UDP services do not support this

groups.label: Exposure
groups.sub: What opens on the server, and where it leads.

groups.label: Website
groups.sub: How the web proxy reaches it.

groups.label: Traffic
groups.sub: Limits and what the target sees.

node.label: Disable encryption of forwarded data
node.help: Disable encryption of forwarded data (authentication still runs)

node.label: Interval
node.help: How often the server and each client check that the other is still there

node.label: Handshake timeout
node.help: Time a new connection has to authenticate

node.label: Max handshakes
node.help: Concurrent connections that have not finished authenticating

node.label: Max connections per client
node.help: Connections this server forwards to one client at once, unless that client has its own Max connections on this server

node.label: Max waiting connections
node.help: Connections waiting for a data channel, per client

node.label: Idle channels kept ready
node.help: Data channels each client keeps open in advance, so a new connection starts without a round trip

node.label: Max idle channels
node.help: Most data channels each client keeps ready; the pool grows toward it when busy and shrinks when idle

node.label: No delay
node.help: Send small writes at once instead of batching them (TCP_NODELAY)

node.label: Keepalive
node.help: Idle time before keepalive probes start; 0 turns them off

node.label: Session timeout
node.help: A UDP peer that sends nothing for this long is forgotten

node.label: Max UDP peers per port
node.help: Most UDP peers one service port keeps at once; a datagram from a new peer beyond it is dropped. For example 20000; the default is 4096

node.label: Metrics endpoint
node.help: Serve Prometheus metrics at /metrics; off unless set

node.label: Listen address
node.help: Address for the metrics endpoint, for example 127.0.0.1:9100; a port alone means 127.0.0.1

groups.label: Web proxy
groups.sub: One HTTPS port for websites and TLS services, told apart by name.

groups.label: This server
groups.sub: What this server may dial for itself, for services with client: self and reach: self.
